evasoes.descricao: Semantic rewording of the hostile request using synonyms, circumlocutions, metaphors or indirect language to evade keyword-based filters while keeping the meaning intact.
Encodes the payload with classic ciphers (ROT13, Caesar, Base64, Morse, A1Z26, ASCII hex, etc.) or asks the model to decode before answering, bypassing filters that operate on plain text.
Translates the payload into a low-resource language or one less represented in safety training, exploiting the fact that safety alignment is weaker in non-English languages.
Uses Unicode homoglyphs, diacritics, invisible (zero-width) characters, font variation (Unicode bold/italic) or markdown/HTML formatting to disguise keywords and evade textual detection.
Splits the hostile payload into harmless fragments distributed across the prompt or across turns, instructing the model to concatenate them to rebuild the full instruction.
Applies deterministic rule-based transformations (Pig Latin, Leetspeak, reversed words, word-level permutation, custom cipher) that the model can reverse internally.
Uses an auxiliary LLM to automatically generate payload variations that preserve meaning but avoid detection, including genetic algorithms over prompts (AutoDAN, GPTFUZZER, TAP).

Exploits tokenizer quirks (compound tokens, glitch tokens, boundary splitting) to create text representations that look harmless at the character level but yield tokens the model interprets differently.
Applies intentional misspellings, scrambling of inner letters (keeping the first and last letters) or abbreviations that humans and LLMs understand but exact-match filters miss.
Embeds the hostile instruction in an alternative modality (image with text, audio, PDF document, video) that the model processes but text filters do not inspect.

Defines a bijective mapping (custom alphabet, invented language, substitution dictionary) between words/characters and their equivalents, encoding the hostile instruction in that mapping and asking the model to decode it.
Hides the hostile instruction using textual steganographic techniques: first letters of each line (acrostic), variable spacing, bold/italic marking, or encoding in image/document metadata.
